tekst: Some families burn an Advent candle down a little every evening in December. What is printed down its side?
fakta: Each evening you burn it down to the next number – by Christmas Eve it's almost gone.

tekst: The more you take, the more you leave behind. What are they?
svar: Footsteps – in the snow, for example!

hint: He wears a red suit and comes down the chimney.

tekst: Cut coloured paper into strips, loop each strip into a ring and link them together into a long chain. Hang it across the room – the longer the better!
tips: A dab of glue or a bit of tape keeps the rings closed.

tekst: An old carol about sailing ships that come in on Christmas morning.
Act out ‘decorating the tree’ or ‘wrapping presents’ without saying a word – the others guess. Charades has its own Christmas category.
What do some families hide in the Christmas pudding for luck?
fakta: Traditionally it was a silver sixpence – whoever finds it is said to have good luck all year. Mind your teeth!

tekst: What gets wetter the more it dries?

hint: Shiny, sparkly strands you drape over the tree.

tekst: Wrap up warm and go for a short evening walk together. Count the Christmas lights in the windows – who spots the most? Maybe you'll see some stars too.
tips: Stay together and stick to well-lit streets.

tekst: A king looks out on the Feast of Stephen and sees a poor man gathering firewood in the snow.
Play Pointy with the Christmas pack: read the statement, count down – and everyone points at once. Perfect round the dinner table.
Robins are on lots of Christmas cards. Why were Victorian postmen nicknamed ‘robins’?
fakta: Postmen in red coats delivered the first Christmas cards – so the robin, with its red breast, ended up on the cards.

tekst: What has hands but can't clap?

hint: He has a carrot for a nose and stays outside all winter.

tekst: Write or draw a kind message to someone in the family. Hide it where they'll find it tomorrow – under a pillow, in a shoe or in a lunchbox.
tips: Whoever finds the note can pass a new one on.

tekst: A true love sends more and more presents – birds, gold rings, dancing ladies – day after day.
valg: We Wish You a Merry Christmas

tekst: Every December a big Christmas tree stands in Trafalgar Square in London. Which country sends it?
fakta: The city of Oslo has sent a tree every year since 1947, as a thank-you for Britain's help during the Second World War.

tekst: Draw who's Secret Santa for whom. The present can be a drawing, a poem or a good deed – the nicest ones are often homemade.

hint: Pull it with someone – bang! – and out falls a paper hat.

tekst: Around 21 December we have the shortest day of the year. What is it called?
fakta: After the solstice the days slowly get longer again – and people gather at Stonehenge to watch the sun rise.

tekst: Carol singers at the door ask for figgy pudding – and say they won't go until they get some!
valg: We Wish You a Merry Christmas

tekst: Which month has 28 days?
svar: All of them! Every month has at least 28 days.

tekst: Light a candle, snuggle up and tell each other about your favourite Christmas memory. And don't forget to leave out a mince pie for Father Christmas – and a carrot for the reindeer!
tips: Thank you for opening the calendar with us. Merry Christmas!
